The papersThe code

Pathway activity from condition-responsive genes, dug back up.

52 results: 4 exact, 7 agree, 33 partly agree, 5 differ, 3 not attempted. The lost method was rebuilt from the paper's Methods, and the seven datasets from GEO, Bioconductor and the GSEA site.

The breast datasets' preprocessing and probe-to-gene mapping are not stated, and our breast data are not the paper's: only 3 of Table S2's 15 CORG lists come back. The source curves (A, C) keep the published shape and order; the verification curves (B, D) differ by up to 0.5. One point is off: PAC_all at 2% reads 2.43 on the figure and 2.55 in our run; the other 19 are within 0.1. One point is off: PAC at 2% reads 1.73 on the figure and 1.37 in our run (the paper's curve rises at 2% and falls again); every other readable point is within 0.1. Boston's top pathways are not those of Tian's statistic on the GSEA Boston file: Table 1's Boston-to-Michigan pathways rank as low as 375th in it. The Boston CORGs themselves are exact (Table 1), so the difference is in which pathways are ranked; our PAC is 0.2 to 0.4 above the figure in G and up to 0.5 below it in H.

PAC_random differs because the paper's random sets skip the CORG search (supported); NF-kB is near 1 for every method in our data (open); the rest differ by up to 0.05 with unstated classifier settings. 5 of 8 bars within 0.02. Boston to Michigan: our PAC is 0.56 against 0.66, because the paper's Boston markers were not Tian's top 52 (with all pathways as input, PAC is 0.71); the Gene bars of both lung directions are 0.02 to 0.03 high. -log10 p of a Wilcoxon test on 500 paired AUCs moves with every unstated setting and with the random partitions; no printed value comes back to its decimal. Where both are significant the sizes are close (Breast Netherlands 19.2 against 16.9); the significance pattern is compared in text.pac_beats_gene_within and _across.

Every result

Every figure, table and claim of the paper. Figure values are read off the published figures (Figs 2 and 3) or the vector supplements (Figs S1 to S5); a value agrees within 0.1 |t| (Fig. 2), 0.02 AUC (Figs 3, S2, S3), 0.05 overlap (Fig. S1) or 50 of 500 classifiers (frequencies).

Port against the authors' codeNot attemptedThe authors' software is lost: no link, no availability statement and no code in the supplement; searches of GitHub, CRAN, Bioconductor, PyPI and the authors' lab pages found nothing (issue #47). pacorg is written from the Methods and checked against the paper.
pacorg, the method as a Python packageAgrees

The main claim, that classifiers on CORG-based pathway activity beat classifiers on genes, holds where our data are the paper's or close to it (Breast Netherlands, Lung Michigan, Lung Boston, Michigan to Boston); it does not hold in our NF-kB, Prostate, Breast USA, USA to Netherlands and Boston to Michigan runs, because our breast and NF-kB data are not the authors' (open) and Boston's pathway pre-selection differs.

What came back

Table 1
All 18 CORG lists and all 18 CORG and member counts, from the GSEA lung files.
Fig. 2
The lung panels E and F within 0.1 at 37 of 39 points; the breast and Boston panels keep the paper's order of curves in the source datasets.
Fig. 4
Glycolysis and estrogen signalling higher in poor prognosis in both lung datasets.
Table 1 frequencies
Michigan to Boston: the paper's eight pathways are our eight most used, in its order but for one swap.
The method
CORG search, pathway activity and Tian's pre-selection, as the Python package pacorg.

What stayed buried

  • The breast data as the authors prepared them: 3 of Table S2's 15 CORG lists come back.
  • Boston's top pathways: the paper's are not those of Tian's statistic on the GSEA Boston file.
  • NF-kB: in our 24 arrays every classifier is near perfect; the paper's gene classifier is at 0.82.
  • How the paper computed the CORG overlap of Fig. S1.

The main claim, that classifiers on CORG-based pathway activity beat classifiers on genes, holds where our data are the paper's or close to it (Breast Netherlands, Lung Michigan, Lung Boston, Michigan to Boston); it does not hold in our NF-kB, Prostate, Breast USA, USA to Netherlands and Boston to Michigan runs, because our breast and NF-kB data are not the authors' (open) and Boston's pathway pre-selection differs.

What we matched

How each part of the paper's method was rebuilt.

Activity
Each gene z-scored over all samples; a set's activity is the sum of member z-scores over sqrt(k).
CORGs
Members ranked by t, added while |t| of the activity rises (pooled-variance t).
Pre-selection
Tian's statistic as sum of t over sqrt(members), top 52 of 522; the Methods say average t, but Table 1 and Fig. 2 follow the standardized sum.
Classifier
Logistic regression; markers added in order of p-value, the count chosen by validation AUC; 100 runs of 5-fold CV.
Data
GSEA lung files as distributed; GEO and Bioconductor for the other five, mapped to MSigDB v1.0 symbols through Entrez Gene IDs.

Pathway activity came back exactly where the paper's own data survive: every CORG list of Table 1.
